prompt.context: Our client, the Toto Foundation, is a new non-profit arm of a well-known drone manufacturing and logistics company that is exploring aid projects in Africa. Our client is seeking your expertise to determine where and how to deploy their technology to have the maximum impact.
prompt.question: Where and how should the Toto Foundation deploy their drone technology in Africa to have the maximum impact?

clarifying_info.q: What does the parent company do?
clarifying_info.a: The parent company manufactures and sells drones. It has extensive commercial experience in the US and uses drones for transportation of light packages and limited military/defense applications.
The foundation has a $4 million upfront grant and $1 million per year thereafter. There are no additional sources of funding.

clarifying_info.q: What are the primary goals and constraints?
clarifying_info.a: Maximize impact on human lives while staying within budget. Safety is the primary concern. The grant can only apply to projects in Africa. Success of this phase will prompt future investment.

exhibits.title: Project Proposals
exhibits.shows: A table listing six potential aid projects with scores for Expertise (1-5), Need (1-5), Impact (1-5 relative to existing solutions), and Upfront Deployment Cost

exhibits.title: Target Country Data
exhibits.shows: A table with population, density, and country size for 5 candidate countries, plus a radar/spider chart comparing each country on Ease of Doing Business, Danger to Nonprofits, Quality of Road Infrastructure, Vaccination Rate, and Poverty Level

exhibits.title: Annual Cost Calculation Inputs
exhibits.shows: A table with operational parameters for Senegal and Guinea: Vials per Flight, Miles per Delivery (Roundtrip), Fuel & Maintenance Cost per Mile, Days of Flying per Year, Total Flights per Day, and Annual Regulatory & Ground Facility Costs

notes: Drone costs are already included in upfront development costs
A biotech firm is donating the vaccines and other medication — no buying or selling of products

framework: Existing Capabilities: drone capabilities and expertise, deployment experience, available funding ($4M upfront, $1M/year)
Priorities: maximize lives impacted, stay within budget constraints (upfront and ongoing)
Personnel/Firm: existing partnerships to leverage, volunteer and staff safety
Target Market: needs (food, medicine, agriculture, security), trends (instability, political changes, unmet needs)
Other Considerations: infrastructure available for technology deployment, regulatory approval and constraints, safety and flight risks

questions.prompt: Which project from Exhibit 1 is the most attractive for the Foundation to pursue?
questions.guidance: Step 1 — eliminate on budget: Blood & Plasma Delivery ($11.5M) and Insulin Delivery ($6.5M) both exceed the $4M upfront grant; eliminate both. Step 2 — eliminate on expertise: Crop Monitoring and Poacher Monitoring both score 1 on expertise; likely operational challenges; eliminate. Step 3 — compare remaining two: Dry Food Delivery (Expertise 4, Need 3, Impact 2, $3.7M) vs. Vaccine & General Medicinal Delivery (Expertise 4, Need 5, Impact 5, $3.8M). Both have similar expertise and upfront cost; Vaccine & General Medicinal Delivery wins on need AND impact. Bonus insight: vaccines are light, easy to transport, simple to administer, and address high unmet need in developing countries. Risks: fragile, temperature-sensitive, supply chain constraints.

questions.prompt: What factors should the Foundation consider when choosing a country to launch vaccine & medicinal delivery? Then, using Exhibit 2, which two countries should be selected?
questions.guidance: Pre-exhibit brainstorm categories — Population: density (drones add value in lower-density areas where road access is poor), total size (large enough to justify investment), demographics (disease susceptibility). Health/Medical: vaccination rate (most benefit in low-vaccinated areas), deaths from preventable diseases. Safety/Other: crime rate and danger to nonprofit workers, ease of doing business. After exhibit: Eliminate Rwanda (relatively high vaccination rates and road quality, lower poverty — lower marginal impact). Eliminate Tanzania (high vaccination rates and road quality, but also HIGH danger to nonprofit workers — safety concern). Eliminate Central African Republic (high need but significant risks: high danger to nonprofits, very low ease of doing business). Select Senegal and Guinea: both have lower vaccination rates, higher poverty, lower road quality (need is high), AND low danger to workers (safety is satisfied). A strong candidate also notes the limitations of the data and asks for country-specific cost and rollout data.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors should the Foundation consider when choosing a country for the vaccine delivery program?

categories.name: Population
ideas: Population density — drones add most value in low-density areas where roads are poor
Total population size — large enough to justify investment
Age and demographic profile — certain populations (children, elderly) more susceptible to vaccine-preventable disease

categories.name: Health / Medical Need
ideas: Current vaccination rate — lower rate means higher marginal impact
Deaths from preventable diseases — proxy for unmet medical need
Availability of existing healthcare infrastructure and alternatives

categories.name: Safety & Security
ideas: Danger level to nonprofit workers and volunteers
Political stability and risk of conflict
Crime rate and likelihood of equipment theft or sabotage

categories.name: Operational & Regulatory
ideas: Ease of doing business — affects likelihood of successful rollout
Quality of road and transportation infrastructure
Availability of local partners and government cooperation

categories.name: Economics
ideas: GDP per capita and poverty level — signal inability to self-fund solutions
Existing foreign aid presence — avoid duplicating efforts
Potential for local cost-sharing or future self-sustainability

recommendation: Launch the vaccine and general medicinal delivery service in Senegal
Senegal offers the highest impact: 300,000 vials delivered per year at an annual cost of $1,000,000 (within the annual grant), compared to 120,000 vials per year at the same cost in Guinea
The upfront deployment cost of $3.8M is within the $4M grant
risks: First international project of this type — untested operational model
Untested vaccine partnership and uncertainty around program costs
Changing regulatory environment for drone flights
Political instability could rapidly shift needs or access
Uncertainty about local infrastructure for administering vaccines upon delivery
next_steps: Launch a pilot program to confirm costs align with estimates
Explore infrastructure-building projects to support drone delivery (acknowledging these are outside current budget scope)
Begin obtaining regulatory approval and expand partnership network in Senegal
Establish a detailed timeline for rollout
Evaluate scalability: Senegal's lower variable cost per flight provides easier path to scale
